summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a number with a fractional part.
description: `nonDouble(value)` is the same test as `!isDouble(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
A synonym of the `Float` family, offered under the name people reach for first. In JavaScript every number already is a double, so `double` names no runtime distinction of its own.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a number with a fractional part; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonDouble(42); // => true
nonDouble(1.0); // => true
nonDouble(Infinity); // => true
nonDouble("1.5"); // => true
nonDouble(1.5); // => false
nonDouble(-0.1); // => false
```
